name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj
subtitle: Maratha · Early modern
brief: SAMPLE · Built an independent Maratha kingdom from hill forts while facing far larger empires.

lessons.heading: Who was Shivaji?
lessons.body:
*SAMPLE text for testing. Not reviewed.*

Shivaji Bhonsle was born in the hill fort of Shivneri, in western India, around 1630. His father served the Sultanate of Bijapur, one of the powers that ruled the Deccan. In his teens Shivaji began taking hill forts near Pune, slowly building a territory of his own.

Over the next thirty years he fought Bijapur, the Mughal Empire and others, often with small, fast forces that knew the hills well. He also built forts along the coast and a navy to protect trade.

In 1674 he was crowned at Raigad fort and took the title Chhatrapati. He ran his state with a council of eight ministers, the Ashta Pradhan. He died in 1680, leaving a kingdom that grew into the Maratha Empire.

- Born: about 1630, Shivneri fort
- Crowned: 1674, Raigad
- Died: 1680

person.role: King (Chhatrapati) and founder of the Maratha state
person.headline: SAMPLE · Turned a few hill forts into a kingdom that stood up to the Mughal Empire.

traits.name: Patient planner
traits.text: SAMPLE · Took and strengthened hill forts one at a time instead of risking everything on one battle.

traits.name: Fast and mobile
traits.text: SAMPLE · Used small, quick forces that knew the hills, striking where enemies were weakest.

traits.name: Builder of institutions
traits.text: SAMPLE · Set up a council of ministers and a regular way to collect revenue, so the state did not rest on him alone.

traits.name: Sea-minded
traits.text: SAMPLE · Built coastal forts and a navy when most land powers in India paid little attention to the sea.

changes.text: SAMPLE · Created the Ashta Pradhan, a council of eight ministers with clear jobs.
SAMPLE · Built a navy and sea forts such as Sindhudurg on the Konkan coast.
SAMPLE · Founded the state that later grew into the Maratha Empire.

odds_beaten.why_impossible: SAMPLE · Bijapur sent a large army under its general Afzal Khan to crush the young ruler.
odds_beaten.outcome: SAMPLE · Shivaji killed Afzal Khan at a meeting near Pratapgad fort, and his forces routed the army.

odds_beaten.why_impossible: SAMPLE · He was held under guard at the Mughal court, far from his own lands.
odds_beaten.outcome: SAMPLE · He escaped, by tradition hidden in baskets of sweets, and went home to rebuild his power.

use_today.text: SAMPLE · Fight on ground where your strengths count. A small team that moves fast and knows the terrain can beat a bigger one.
